why: The doc sentence is real and verbatim (remote-control.md line 263, and the page is a legitimate Claude contract page - row 150 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv). The repo facts are also broadly right: apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:105 carries the three-reason union, :116-117 is the only presence branch, and `grep -rain -e 'CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE' -e 'presenceFile' -e 'presence_file'` over packages/ apps/ returns 0 hits, as does a sweep for powerMonitor / getSystemIdleTime / getSystemIdleState / screen-lock. The finding is nevertheless refuted on subsystem and product-scope grounds. (1) WRONG SUBSYSTEM - the sibling-symbol trap. The quoted line sits under '## Mobile push notifications' on the Remote Control page and governs pushes delivered to your PHONE via the Claude mobile app while a Remote Control session runs on your machine. CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE exists precisely BECAUSE the delivery target is a second device: the CLI cannot otherwise tell whether you are at your desk in another window. Our `deliverModelNotification` (the claim names it `showAgentNotification`, which has 0 hits repo-wide) is the desktop-shell backend of the `PushNotification` TOOL, cited to `tools-reference.md:41` and described in packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:628 as 'Raise an OS notification on the user's desktop'. It is an Electron Notification on the SAME machine, reached via packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/push-notification.ts -> deliverDesktopNotification. Same-machine delivery and cross-device delivery are different subsystems with different presence semantics. (2) THE CONSEQUENCE IS FALSE, AND INVERTED. Read the whole line: the doc's own recommended wiring is 'create the file when your screen unlocks and delete it when your screen locks'. Applied to a local desktop notification that rule suppresses the banner exactly when the screen is unlocked and the banner would be SEEN, and delivers it exactly when the screen is locked and nobody is there. Window focus is the correct and only meaningful gate for a same-machine notification; if the user is away, the banner simply waits on that machine and reaches nobody remotely. Importing the gate would be a defect, not parity. (3) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. Remote Control requires 'Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported', and as of v2.1.196 is explicitly disabled when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a host other than api.anthropic.com, 'such as an LLM gateway or proxy' - which is exactly this fork's architecture (the Nestor corporate gateway). The fork implements no Remote Control whatsoever: grep for 'remote-control' across packages/shared/src, packages/server-core/src, packages/server/src, apps/electron/src and apps/cli/src returns zero files; the only RemoteControl* symbols in the tree are codex-protocol generated types for Codex's own unrelated feature. The capability intake fixture records the exclusion by name - packages/pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/extension-first/fixtures/claude-code-2.1.218.json:414 lists 'mobile-remote-control-delivery' in `exclusions`, alongside 'anthropic-account-brokering' and 'agent-teams'. A presence gate for a mobile-push channel the product does not have is not a divergence. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (checked; none touch notifications), but it is a scope exclusion of the same kind.
correctedState: Our PushNotification path is a LOCAL desktop notification on the machine hosting the session, not a cross-device mobile push. `deliverModelNotification` (apps/electron/src/main/notifications.ts:100; the finding's `showAgentNotification` does not exist) gates on window focus, the notifications setting, and platform support, and reads no presence-marker file - correctly, because CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE answers 'is the human at the host machine', a question that only matters when the notification travels to a second device. For a same-machine banner the doc's own screen-unlock wiring would invert the tool's purpose: suppress when visible, deliver when nobody is watching. The fork additionally ships no Remote Control at all - it is claude.ai-subscription-only and disabled behind an LLM gateway or proxy, i.e. behind this fork's Nestor gateway - and the capability intake fixture excludes 'mobile-remote-control-delivery' by name.
